newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCA AND ATLETICO KEEP UP THE SCORING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCA AND ATLETICO KEEP UP THE SCORING.

text.p: Barcelona and Atletico Madrid lived up to their no-holds-barred reputations on Saturday when they shared a 3-3 draw in a roller-coaster Spanish first division clash in Nou Camp.
The lead changed hands three times in a match that had always promised goals.

Barcelona had beaten the defending champions 5-3 in the traditional league curtain-raiser and triumphed 5-3 and 4-3 in the corresponding league fixtures of the 1993-94 and 1994-95 seasons. Atletico won here 3-1 last season.
Atletico opened the scoring after just six minutes through Spain midfielder Jose Luis Caminero, playing only his second game since returning from injury.
The Barcelona defence back-pedalled into their own area, Toni Munoz swung in a left-foot cross and Caminero buried a downward header firmly in the back of Fransesc Arnau's net.
It was a rude introduction to life in the Barcelona first team for 21-year-old Arnau, who was drafted into the side after Barcelona's three regular squad 'keepers were ruled out.
Arnau usually plays for second division side Barcelona B and was named in the first team just hours before kick-off.
Barcelona surged forward in search of a swift equaliser and pulled level through Juan Pizzi after 15 minutes.
The Argentine-born Spanish international neatly pulled down a pass form Sergi Barjuan, turned his marker inside the penalty area and sidefooted the ball past goalkeeper Jose Molina.
A quarter of an hour later the Catalans, playing without a number of key players including Brazilian sensation Ronaldo and Bulgarian striker Hristo Stoichkov, stole the lead through a fortunate goal.
Luis Enrique Martinez, who wreaked havoc down the right wing in the first half, broke down the touchline and looked up to see Pizzi surging into the box to receive a cross.

The former Real Madrid player tried to pick Pizzi out, but his centre skewed off the outside of his boot and entered the net off the left-hand post of Molina, who had come off his line in anticipation of a cross.
The second half was just as evenly balanced and equally eventful.

Kiko Narvaez forced Arnau to make a fine save with a header from a cross from Caminero and Brazil's Giovanni and Romanian Gheorghe Popescu both came close for the home side, who constantly threatened to extend their lead.
But it was Atletico who struck next through Juan Vizcaino, who killed a floated cross from Esnaider with his right foot and slotted the ball home under Arnau to make the score 2-2.
The champions took the lead for the second time in the match from a highly controversial penalty.

Caminero and Esnaider bustled into the Barcelona penalty area with the ball, Caminero tried to pull the ball back onto his right foot to shoot and French international defender Laurent Blanc ran into him.

Although it was dificult to see what Blanc could have done to avoid the clash, the referee pointed to the spot and Esnaider slammed the ball home to make the score 3-2, threatening Barcelona's 11-match unbeaten run.
A spate of substitutions followed as Atletico tried to bolster their defence and Barcelona sought an equaliser.
The shaven-headed Ivan de la Pena came on for Barca, as did veteran club captain Jose Maria Bakero, playing maybe his last game for the Catalans before moving to Mexico.
And it was de la Pena who made the opening for Giovanni to equalise, rounding off an astonishing match.
De la Pena's precise pass put Pizzi through on goal, his shot was blocked and the 24-year-old Brazilian coolly tucked home the rebound.
Barcelona have now scored an average of three goals per game in their first 12 matches and they lead the table by three points from Real Madrid, who have a game in hand.
Atletico stay sixth on 18 points, but showed on Saturday they are far from ready to relinquish their hard-won league championship title.
"The draw was a tribute to the football played by both side," Atletico coach Radomir Antic said.

Barcelona coach Bobby Robson said he was satisfied with the way his side had played: "We were losing the game, then controlling it, then letting it slip again. The public have seen a marvellous match and I can't complain about the result."
Teams:

Barcelona - 28-Francesc Arnau, 3-Abelardo Fernandez (23-Ivan de la Pena 74th), 4-Josep Guardiola, 5-Gheorghe Popescu (captain), 10-Giovanni, 12-Sergi Barjuan, 15-Laurent Blanc, 19- Juan Pizzi, 20-Miguel Nadal, 21-Luis Enrique Martinez, 27-Roger (6-Jose Maria Bakero 79th)

Atletico Madrid - 1-Jose Molina, 3-Toni Munoz, 4-Roberto Solozabal (captain), 5-Juan Lopez, 6-Santi Denia, 8-Juan Vizcaino, 9-Juan Esnaider, 10-Milinko Pantic (15-Carlos Aguilera 80th), 14-Diego Simeone, 19-Kiko Narvaez, 21-Jose Luis Caminero (2-Pablo Alfaro 74th)
